key_insight: Regularized policy mirror descent can be made fast and globally convergent even with only one TD critic update per step, including a stochastic single-trajectory version with provable sample complexity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical reinforcement-learning optimization recipe that reduces evaluation overhead and avoids resets, generative models, and nested policy-evaluation loops.
method: Exact coordinate-wise Bellman updates give linear convergence with any positive actor stepsize.
A persistent critic is advanced by one TD update and analyzed via a resolvent-based auxiliary distribution.
The stochastic variant uses strongly convex mirror maps, finite-batch TD, and visitation-weighted error propagation bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports global linear convergence for the deterministic case and an expected value gap of ε after ~O(1/((1−γ)^5 σ̃_b ε)) transitions in the stochastic case.
watch_item: Performance depends on behavior-policy coverage σ̃_b and discount factor γ, so weak coverage or γ close to 1 can make sample complexity large.
paper_title: Fast Regularized Policy Mirror Descent with One-Step TD Updates
